title: Activation-addition Mirror basis
hypothesis: A shared rank-4 activation-steering basis plus per-behavior low-description Givens Views stores fixed-norm steering behaviors with fewer actual bytes than explicit vectors and generic rank-4 coefficients while preserving on-target efficacy and off-target specificity.
physical_object: One shared synthetic 64x4 orthonormal activation basis and one rank-4 seed vector
mirror_coordinate: Two per-behavior Givens angles over the seed vector; optional charged private residual
controls: Shared basis plus FP32 rank-4 coefficient table
Shared basis plus FP16 rank-4 coefficient table
Shared basis plus seed vector and two FP16 Givens angles per behavior
Mirror plus per-behavior FP16 rank-4 private residual

metrics: decode/application wall time and MAC proxy

development.allowed: No hyperparameter selection; run development only to validate deterministic encode/decode and the common fixed shared object.

success_gate: For every rho=0 fresh world: vector NRMSE <=0.01, efficacy >=0.99, off-target drift <=0.01, and actual bytes <=80% of both explicit vectors and the cheapest generic coefficient control.
failure_gate: Aligned quality/byte gate fails or a generic coefficient control dominates.

amendment_A1.reason: A shared physical basis/seed must be the same object across independent development/fresh behavior banks; fitting a new basis per world would confound behavior-code compression with per-world model storage.
amendment_A1.change: Use a deterministic shared synthetic basis and seed vector generated from a fixed public construction seed. Charge both in every payload. Development validates the encoder; no fitting or tuning is performed on fresh behavior vectors.

boundaries: Synthetic fixed-norm Givens steering orbit only.
No pretrained language model or natural behavior steering claim.
All fresh behavior codes are serialized and charged; combination count is not capacity.
